papers_read.title_as_printed: Explainable machine learning models for identifying mild cognitive impairment in older patients with chronic pain (Zhang et al., BMC Nursing 2025)
Mild Cognitive Impairment: Data-Driven Prediction, Risk Factors, and Workup (Fouladvand, Noshad, Goldstein, Periyakoil, Chen; Stanford)

what_each_reports.P-307: Cross-sectional: 612 older (>=60) chronic-pain inpatients in one Chinese pain department, 169 (27.6%) with MCI (Petersen/IWG criteria incl. MoCA<26, neurologist-confirmed); 7 predictors (age, education, pain sites, pain duration, VAS pain level, GDS-15 depression, PSQI sleep); 70/30 split with SMOTETomek on training; XGBoost test AUC 0.925 (95% CI 0.863-0.995), accuracy 0.883.
what_each_reports.P-165: Prognostic: 531,387 primary-care visits of patients >=65 in Stanford EHR (OMOP), label = at least one MCI diagnosis code within one year after the visit; 480 structured and clinical-note concepts; temporal split (train <=2019, test 2020+); random forest test ROC-AUC 68.2 +/- 0.7, XGBoost 66.8, logistic regression 57.0.

quantity_a: ROC-AUC for identifying prevalent MCI (research-criteria diagnosis at assessment) in older chronic-pain patients from seven questionnaire/clinical variables, random internal hold-out.
quantity_b: ROC-AUC for predicting a recorded MCI diagnosis code within the next year from routine EHR history at a primary-care visit, all patients >=65, temporal hold-out.
incompatible_if_same: If the estimands were the same the gap (0.925, CI 0.863-0.995 vs 0.682 +/- 0.7) would exclude each other, but they are not: one is present-status identification with a structured cognitive work-up population, the other is one-year incidence of a billing diagnosis in unselected primary care.

gates.task: mismatch: cross-sectional MCI identification (P-307) vs one-year-ahead MCI onset prediction (P-165); the registry codes P-165 as T2.
gates.dataset_family: mismatch: single-centre Nanchang pain-department cohort vs Stanford Healthcare OMOP EHR (record itself: dataset_equal No).
gates.validation_tier: mismatch in kind: random 70/30 split vs temporal split (train to 2019, test 2020+).
gates.modality_family: both clinical/tabular, but predictor sets entirely different (pain, depression and sleep scales vs 480 EHR diagnosis/medication/procedure/note concepts).

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible: both ROC-AUC, but endpoints differ (prevalent research-criteria MCI vs incident coded MCI diagnosis within one year) and populations differ (chronic-pain inpatients vs all primary-care visits).
performance_validity: flag not tripped (0.925 < 0.97; n=612 with a 184-patient test set).
grounds: P-307 identifies MCI present at assessment in chronic-pain inpatients, whereas P-165 predicts a recorded MCI diagnosis within one year of a primary-care visit, so the endpoint and horizon differ.
The outcome definitions differ: research criteria with MoCA<26 and neurologist confirmation vs any MCI diagnosis code in the EHR.
Populations, predictor sets and validation designs differ, and the task and dataset gates fail with no waiver on record.

evidence_quotes.quote: The outcome of this study was the occurrence of MCI, which was diagnosed according to Petersen's Criteria and the International Working Group on MCI
the XGBoost model performed best, achieving an accuracy of 0.883 and an AUC of 0.925 (95% CI 0.863-0.995).
Each primary care visit was assigned with a binary label indicating if the patient has at least one MCI diagnosis code within one year follow up from the time of their primary care visit
The random forest model has a higher ROC-AUC (68.2%+/-0.7%) than xgboost and logistic regression models on the test set.

record_defects: Both claims labelled 'T1', but P-165 is a one-year-ahead prediction of MCI onset (registry codes it T2).
task_equivalence true / dataset_family_equivalence true contradict dataset_equal 'No' within the same record.
Index registry row for P-165 gives Best_Metric 'not reported'; the paper reports test ROC-AUC 68.2 +/- 0.7.
resolution_status 'partially_resolved_candidate' rests on a generic list of 'bridging' papers with no separating condition.
what_would_change_the_verdict: Nothing within these two papers: P-165 reports no cross-sectional identification result and P-307 no incident-diagnosis result.
